summary: Tomoyuki Uno works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He was affiliated with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 1998) and served as an assistant professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000-2006).
Tomoyuki Yamakami studied under Stephen Cook and Alasdair Urquhart from circa 1993 to 1997.

Tomy Augustine is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He earned a master's degree at the University of Madras, studied under C. S. Sundaram, and completed a PhD at Banaras Hindu University under Munni K. Agrawal. He was attested at Salesian College in 2008.

Toni Huber specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Jim Wilson, earning a PhD at the University of Canterbury by 1993 under Paul Harrison and William S. Sax. He held professorships at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 2000) and Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 2006-2008).

Tony K. Stewart is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Western Kentucky University (~1972-1976). He taught in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at North Carolina State University (~1986-2011) and held a post at Vanderbilt University around 2011.

Torkel Brekke works in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MPhil at the University of Oslo (~1990-1995) under Jens Braarvig and Georg von Simson, and completed doctoral studies at Oxford (1996-1999) under Richard Gombrich. He has held positions at Oslo, PRIO, and OsloMet.

Toru Funayama works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology. He studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner (1991-1992). He served as associate professor at Kyushu University (attested 1999-2003) and professor at Kyoto University and its Institute for Research in Humanities.

Toru Haneda (1882-1955) specialized in Iranian/Central Asian studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. After studying at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, he served in multiple posts at Kyoto University from 1909 onward, including professor, dean, and director, and later headed the Academy of Oriental Culture.

Toru Kumeji specializes in Buddhist studies and computational humanities. He has held posts at the National Institute for Digital Humanities and at the Institute of Humanities Information Studies (attested 2015) as a senior researcher.

Toru Sagara (1921-2000) was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1941-1944) under Tetsuro Watsuji, and later held posts at Ibaraki University (~1950-1963), the University of Tokyo (~1963-1982), and Kyoritsu Women's University (~1982-1997).

Toru Takahashi (1878-1967) worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. A University of Tokyo graduate, he served in Korea as a teacher and principal, later becoming a professor at Keijo Imperial University (1926-1940), Fukuoka University (1949), and Tenri University (1950-1964).

Toru Tomabechi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1985-1990) and the University of Lausanne (~1992-2001), where he was also an assistant. He later held senior researcher posts at the Institute of Humanities Information Studies and the National Institute for Digital Humanities.
Toshiaki Yamada is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He studied at Toyo University from circa 1966 to 1976 and held an academic post there from circa 1978 to 2017.

Toshifumi Goto is an Indology and linguistics scholar. After earning a PhD from the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (-1982) and studying under several scholars including Karl Hoffmann, he held professorships at Osaka University and Tohoku University (attested 2003-2012).
Toshihide Unebe is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Issai Funahashi and served as a professor at Doho University (attested 1991).

Toshihiko Izutsu (1914-1993) worked in philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. A Keio University graduate, he held a chair there (1954-1981), along with posts at McGill University (1961, 1969-1975) and a professorship at the Iranian Research Institute of Philosophy (1975-1979).

Toshihiko Kimura is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Tohoku University (~1959-1963), he taught there part-time, served as assistant professor at Tokai Gakuin University (~1979-1989), and became professor emeritus at Shitennoji University (~2006).
Toshihiro Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor (attested 1963) and later as a professor (attested 1976) at Shuchiin University.

Toshihiro Wada works in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981 and held an academic post, including as assistant professor, at Nagoya University from circa 1990 to 2020.

Toshiichi Endo is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Kelaniya and a doctoral thesis at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (-1995), supervised by Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake.
